newsitem.title: UK: Mark steady in Europe as tight ranges prevail.
newsitem.headline: Mark steady in Europe as tight ranges prevail.

text.p: The mark was mostly steady on it European crosses in morning trade, creeping above overnight lows but finding little impetus to break out of its recent ranges.
Lower-than-expected inflation data out of France and Spain kept the rate cut argument simmering for those countries, lifting their bond markets but having little impact on the currencies.

Comments from Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli this morning calling for a broad-based start to monetary union which included Italy, Spain and Portugal kept the recent EMU optimism alive. This provided some support for the lira, peseta and escudo but narrow ranges continued to prevail.
"Those comments really back up the market view that EMU is going ahead and is likely to be broad," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International in London.
BoF's Marchelli believed Germany wanted an excessively strong euro and a broad-based EMU resulting in a weaker euro would be good for employment in Europe.

Italy Prime Minister Romano Prodi said today Italy was creating the conditions to participate at EMU's start but warned Italy needed political stability to get there, referring to his hard-left allies' split with the government over the motion to send forces to Albania.
Prodi easily survived a Senate confidence vote late Thursday over the deployment of troops to Albania and is likely to survive Saturday's lower house vote.
Mark/lira was trading at 987.70/8.00 against 989.55/85 late Thursday in Europe.

Mark/French franc was also steady, edging back above a fresh 45-month low set overnight. The franc shrugged off lower-than-expected March CPI data which showed a monthly rise of 0.1 percent and a 1.1 percent rise year-on-year, a 30-year low, said analysts.

"Whilst this will offer some support to the bond market, the figures -- along with yesterday's consumer confidence survey -- show the French economy is far from buoyant and should limit any downside pressure on mark/French franc," said Nick Parsons, currency strategist at Paribas in London.
Spanish March CPI was also softer than expected with the headline figure up 0.1 percent and up 2.2 percent for the year. Core CPI posted a 0.2 percent rise and increased 2.1 percent for the year.

"The data seem to indicate another rate cut is overdue and we could see another 25 basis points cut in the repo next Tuesday," said Ian Gunner, international economist at Chase Investment Bank, speaking on Reuters Financial Television.
The Bank of Spain holds its next regular repo tender next Tuesday. The repo rate currently stands at 5.75 percent and was last cut by 25 basis points on March 14.
Mark/peseta was easier from Thursday levels, trading at 84.39/42 from 84.44/46.

The Portuguese escudo was also firmer against the mark, finding support from optimism over the country's economy and growing speculation the Bank of Portugal will trim rates today when it announces terms for the next commercial bank reserve period.
Mark/escudo stood at 100.05/08 against 100.13/16 late Thursday in Europe.
